# /dev on a Mac, in readdir order. There is no /dev/serial/by-id on macOS, so only the top level
# matters. Hand-made, modelled on a real machine: an ArduPilot board on USB CDC (cu./tty.usbmodem),
# an FTDI adapter (cu./tty.usbserial), the Bluetooth and debug ports every Mac has, some terminals
# (ttys*) and legacy BSD ptys (ttyp*), and nodes no port list should show. Serial numbers invented.
#
# Entry lines: an absolute path; a directory ends in "/".
/dev/cu.usbmodem14101
/dev/tty.usbmodem14101
/dev/cu.usbserial-A10K3Z9B
/dev/tty.usbserial-A10K3Z9B
/dev/cu.Bluetooth-Incoming-Port
/dev/tty.Bluetooth-Incoming-Port
/dev/cu.debug-console
/dev/tty.debug-console
/dev/ttys001
/dev/ttys000
/dev/ttyp1
/dev/ttyp0
/dev/ptmx
/dev/console
/dev/tty
/dev/fd/
/dev/disk0
/dev/urandom
/dev/random
/dev/zero
/dev/null
